sections.title: Growth and leaves
sections.text: Common spinach is an annual or biennial herb, typically about 25–50 cm tall. It forms a rosette of long-stalked, triangular to oval leaves; its small greenish flowers appear on a flowering stem.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The leaves are widely eaten raw or cooked. Kew records the species as a food plant; the sources consulted do not support a specific toxicity claim for this concise account.
